import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 288

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
-/

namespace Erdos288

/--
Is it true that there are only finitely many pairs of intervals $I_1$, $I_2$ such that
$$
\sum_{n_1 \in I_1} \frac{1}{n_1} + \sum_{n_2 \in I_2} \frac{1}{n_2} \in \mathbb{N}?
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite { I : Fin 2 → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
    ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin 2, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

/--
This is still open even if $|I_2| = 1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.i2_card_eq_1 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite { (I, n₂) : (ℕ+ × ℕ+) × ℕ+ |
    I.1 ≤ I.2 ∧ ∃ n : ℕ+, ∑ n₁ ∈ Set.Icc I.1 I.2, (n₁⁻¹ : ℚ) + (n₂⁻¹ : ℚ) = n } := by
  sorry

/--
It is perhaps true with two intervals replaced by any $k$ intervals.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.k_intervals : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
    ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true for any $k > 2$ that only finitely many $k$ intervals satisfy this condition?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.exists_k_gt_2 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ k > 2, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
      ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
        ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

end Erdos288

reformulations.difference: The integer witness is quantified inside `∀ j`, and ranges over positive naturals rather than the source's natural numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The full double sum is independent of the outer j. Since Fin 2 is nonempty, `∀ j, A j ∧ ∃ n, S = n` is equivalent to `(∀ j, A j) ∧ ∃ n, S = n`: extract the witness at j = 0, or reuse a single witness for every j. Valid intervals have positive endpoints and are nonempty, so their reciprocal sums are positive; consequently a natural-number total is automatically positive. These predicate and finiteness equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The generalization quantifies over all natural k, including zero, and retains the integer witness inside the interval-validity quantifier.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For k > 0, the same quantifier-reordering and positivity arguments recover the usual condition that all k intervals are valid and their combined sum is a natural number. For k = 0, the predicate is vacuous, but its ambient function type `Fin 0 → ℕ+ × ℕ+` has exactly one element, so the required finiteness holds automatically. Thus the full universal statement is equivalent to the source's generalization over positive numbers of intervals. The complete equivalence is proved as Review288.all_k_iff in the scratch file.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. In the singleton variant, Mathlib's summation precedence places `+ (n₂⁻¹ : ℚ)` outside the sum; there is no missing-parentheses defect. Its equivalence to the main predicate with I₂ = {n₂} was proved, and the source's example [3,6] with {20} was verified. The separately named existential extension is a legitimate weaker question, equivalent to the three-interval case: padding with singleton intervals {1} injects solutions for fewer intervals into solutions for more. This equivalence was also proved without using the file's sorry-backed theorems. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully. The source still records the problem as OPEN and explicitly says the singleton case remains open. The problem page and complete LaTeX view were retrieved through a text reader; attempts to retrieve forum comments remained blocked or rate-limited. No repository files were edited.
